historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run nominal BRL revenue growth (volume ~1% + BRL inflation ~3-4%), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every historical CAGR describes the steel cycle, not a trend. The 5y window starts at the FY2020 trough and the 3y window at the FY2022 peak, so revenue reads +9.8% or -5.4% and EPS -12.9% or -52.7% depending on the endpoint. Equity CAGR (5.1%/11.7%) diverges far more than 30% from both and is inflated by BRL depreciation on foreign-subsidiary translation. None is used as a growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (equity-award taxes zero, interest income not stripped since net debt). The owner-FCF CAGR is only marginally below reported (-46.9% vs -44.6% over 3y) because SBC is ~0.2% of revenue; the collapse is the cycle plus the FY2023-25 capex programme (capex rose from 4-5% of revenue to 9.8%), not dilution.

scenario_narratives.base: Section 232 stays broadly in place through the USMCA review but the North American spread drifts off its 2026 high as domestic capacity (including Gerdau's own Midlothian expansion) fills the tariff gap. Brazil stays import-pressured, with record ~40% regional penetration contained rather than reversed by the TRQ regime (renewed to June 2027), and the restructuring plan stops the bleeding without restoring FY2021-23 margins. Miguel Burnier and the other mining projects add R$1.4-1.5bn of EBITDA that is largely independent of the steel cycle, and capex drops from R$6.85bn to the R$4.7bn plan and then to roughly maintenance-plus. The ex-JV EBITDA margin settles at 14.5% through the cycle.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 50% Section 232 tariff proves durable and data-centre, grid and renewables construction keeps NA utilisation and beam/SBQ pricing high. Brazil's trade defence is tightened and extended past 2027 while Selic cuts (from ~13.5%) revive construction, lifting the Brazil BD from ~11% EBITDA margin back toward its 15%+ history. Mining ramps on schedule. The ex-JV margin holds at 16.5-17%, still well below the FY2021-22 peak of 25-30%, on 5-6% nominal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Section 232 is cut or carved out (USMCA settlement, Canada/Mexico exemptions, or a broader tariff reversal) and NA, ~62% of FY2025 EBITDA, loses most of its tariff spread. Chinese exports keep Brazilian utilisation near 35% and the TRQ lapses or is diluted in 2027, forcing further capacity closures on top of Recife/Aconorte. Revenue stalls for two years and the ex-JV margin falls to 11-11.5%, about the FY2018-19 level, with capex held at maintenance-plus because the mining projects are already sunk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF in BRL, converted to USD at spot. The point is to price Gerdau on what the mill network earns through a cycle, not on the 2026 tariff-boosted North American spread or the 2025 impairment-hit year. The ex-JV EBITDA margin is the one driver that matters; capex, tax, leases and working capital are anchored to the FY2025 cash-flow statement and the approved 2026 investment plan.
key_risks_to_valuation: Section 232 tariff policy: each 1pp of mid-cycle ex-JV margin is worth roughly US$0.35-0.40 per ADR
BRL/USD: the USD value moves one-for-one with the BRL rate, and about 60% of EBITDA is USD-earned, so a weaker BRL partly offsets itself in the flows
Brazilian tax contingencies (ICMS, goodwill amortisation, foreign-profit taxation), worth billions of reais and partly unreserved, are not in the bridge
Capex discipline: if the 'competitiveness' budget stays at 2023-25 levels (8-10% of revenue) instead of 5.5%, value falls about 25%
Balance sheet is from 2025-12-31; the 2026 buyback and H1-26 cash generation are not reflected

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (GGB, NYSE) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.13-5.18. FX from Yahoo BRL=X; parity against GGBR4.SA.
data_sources.financials: Gerdau FY2016-FY2025 Form 20-F (IFRS, R$ thousands, converted to millions) via GGB_Metrics.csv and the FY2025 20-F cash-flow statement, debt table, segment note (Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation) and lease note.
data_sources.qualitative: GGB_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q2-26 results, 2026 buyback, Section 232 / Brazil TRQ status, Miguel Burnier mining guidance.

sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py tripped on P/E and P/B because of the known fx_rate direction conflict (memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict): it multiplies the USD ADR price history by inputs.fx_rate (BRL->USD, 0.19149) instead of converting it to BRL, so every historical multiple is understated by ~5.22^2 = 27x (historical P/B 0.02-0.05x, P/E 0.5x), and its implied multiples divide the USD IV by BRL book/EPS (understated 5.22x). Recomputed by hand in BRL: weighted IV US$3.86 / 0.19149 = R$20.2 per share. Implied P/B = 20.2 x 1,975.1 / 53,585 = 0.74x vs a corrected 10yr band of ~0.53-1.30x (avg ~0.91x) -> inside the band. Implied P/E on FY2025 owner EPS (R$0.63, depressed by the R$1.96bn Brazil impairment) is 32x; on impairment-adjusted owner EPS (~R$1.28) it is ~15.7x vs a corrected ex-outlier 10yr average of ~13x -> inside the 2x rule. Implied EV/Adjusted EBITDA ex-JV (EV ~R$44.3bn ex-JV stake over R$9.15bn EBITDA less SBC) is ~4.8x, in line with steel mid-cycle multiples; the market price is ~5.6x. Conclusion: the trip is a checker comparison-basis defect, not a driver error, so drivers were NOT changed (per the memory note's instruction). Needs the maintainer fix to pick one fx_rate direction.

inputs.share_count_basis: 717.36M common + 1,257.78M preferred outstanding net of treasury at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 20-F share reconciliation, GGB_Annual_FY2025.txt:11424). Common and preferred treated as economically equal (one ADR = one preferred share). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 2026 buyback (up to 55M pref + 1.44M common, ~31% done at Q2-26, roughly 17M shares) would cut the count ~1% but is not modelled because no 2026 balance sheet is extracted.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow statement, 'Long-term incentive plans' add-back R$149.2M (GGB_Annual_FY2025.txt:6809). No net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.fx_note: Model in BRL, outputs converted to USD at 1/5.2223 = 0.19149 USD per BRL (Yahoo BRL=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-03T09:58Z). Parity check against the B3 line: GGBR4.SA close (2026-10-02, R$26.10) / 5.2223 = US$4.998 against the GGB NYSE close at inputs.price_as_of, a 0.25% tie, which confirms rate, direction and the 1 ADR = 1 preferred share basis. GGBR3 (common, R$22.55) trades about 14% below GGBR4; the per-share value here is per preferred share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are BRL, so the rate is BRL-denominated: a USD cost of capital of ~9.5-10% for a cyclical steel producer (US 10y ~4.3%, beta ~1.2, ERP 5%, ~1pp blended country premium because ~60% of EBITDA and 56% of gross debt are USD-linked), grossed up by the long-run BRL-USD inflation differential (~2pp; BCB target 3% with tolerance, realized ~4-4.5%) to 12.0%. Terminal growth 4.0% nominal BRL (~0-1% real). Brazil's 10y prefixed yield (~13.5%) is not used directly because most of the earnings are USD. Cyclicality and tariff risk are priced in the scenarios and weights, NOT in the rate: one WACC across all three scenarios (charging risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY2025 lease cash of R$610M (principal 'Leasing payment' 487.8 + interest 122.3, GGB_Annual_FY2025.txt:6852 and :6834) = 0.87% of revenue deducted via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (the company's net-debt figure already excludes them). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 3,683.6 less ROU depreciation 495.5 = 3,188.1, 4.56% of revenue, note 13 line 10044), so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI deducted once in the bridge at book (R$213.1M, FY2025 balance sheet line 8688). NCI profit share is ~R$27-77M/yr, about 2% of net income.
inputs.jv_treatment: EBITDA path excludes the proportional JV/associate EBITDA that Gerdau puts in its Adjusted EBITDA (R$771.9M in FY2025; mainly the North America JVs in Mexico/Canada and Diaco Colombia). The matching asset, investments in associates and JVs at book (R$3,944.5M, segment note line 11829), is added in the equity bridge. Matching-asset rule satisfied.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'; adaptations applied: currency, leases, NCI, JV matching asset). Gerdau is an operating steel producer, not a financial or asset vehicle, so owner-FCF is the right family; the cyclicality is handled by normalising the EBITDA margin to a through-cycle level instead of capitalising FY2025 (impairment-hit, NI R$1.4bn) or FY2021-22 (supercycle, NI R$11-15bn). EBITDA basis: consolidated Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING proportional JV EBITDA = 10,073.7 - 771.9 = R$9,301.8M = 13.3% of FY2025 revenue (FY2024 14.9%, FY2023 ~17.4% ex JV). The 2025 impairment (R$1,964.5M, Brazil assets) is non-cash and sits outside EBITDA. Reported FCF (OCF 7,987.5 - PP&E and intangibles capex 6,852.8 = 1,134.6) is AFTER interest paid (Gerdau classifies interest in operating activities) and includes +R$253M of net short-term-investment sales; the component flows are unlevered and pre-interest, so net debt is deducted once. Interest income is not stripped (net debt, not net cash). Capex: FY2025 R$6.85bn was the peak of the Miguel Burnier mining / Ouro Branco programme; the Board approved R$4.7bn for 2026 (GGB_Annual_FY2025.txt:6382), with maintenance about R$3bn/yr. Buyback status: an active repurchaser (R$1.17bn FY2025, R$1.19bn FY2024), far above the R$149M SBC charge, so the flat count is more than funded. Working capital: cash-conversion cycle 77 days at Dec-25, so receivables + inventory - payables are ~21% of revenue; wc_capture -20 (growth consumes cash). Net debt and shares are from the FY2025 20-F (2025-12-31); no 2026 interim is extracted. Analysis.json cites ND/EBITDA ~0.69x at Q2-26, which implies a similar ~R$8bn net debt.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3%: North American USD volumes and prices up post-Section 232, offset by the BRL strengthening (USD/BRL ~5.2 vs a ~5.6 FY2025 average) that shrinks translated NA revenue; Brazil flat. Then 4% nominal BRL.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 15.5% ex-JV (Q2-26 Adjusted EBITDA ~R$3.4bn incl JV, the best since Q3-23). Fades to a 14.5% mid-cycle by year 3: the ex-JV margin averaged ~14% over FY2017-25 excluding the FY2021-22 supercycle, plus ~1.5-2pp of structural mining EBITDA (Miguel Burnier, R$1.4-1.5bn at full ramp), minus partial normalisation of the tariff-inflated NA spread.
base.capex_rationale: R$4.7bn approved 2026 plan (~6.5% of revenue), stepping down to 5.5% = ~R$3bn maintenance (4.3%) plus ~1.2% competitiveness capex.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Cash taxes ran ~17-20% of operating EBIT FY2023-25 (JCP interest-on-capital deductions in Brazil, 21% US federal rate on the NA majority of profit). 22% is a modest normalisation.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 12%/4% is 13x terminal FCF; the 12x cap (bottom of the method's 12-15x cyclical band) binds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the majority of group EBITDA now depends on a single regulator's trade policy (Section 232, with the USMCA review live) and Brazil's TRQ protection expires June 2027. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right: tariffs held, Brazilian trade defence tightened, and a Selic-led construction recovery. Base at 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
